history.notes: Three small frictions fixed: every date field now takes '27/10', '15 Nov', '28th' and the like (not only full dates), including the Analysis custom range; the Plan header shows an Undo link for two minutes after you remove a row; and the Bills table's Priority and Frequency are one readable 'fortnightly · essential' column.

A quieter, more professional look: one hairline border on every card (no coloured outlines), no decorative accent bars, a flat slimmer top bar, a title-only navigation rail that fits a laptop screen, neutral badges, plain table rows and pills, and Plan rows with a tidy ⋯ menu for Edit and Remove. Nothing was removed.

Gerald now asks what you pay for: a bill interview (rent, power, phone, insurance, streaming, gym and more) one question at a time. Say yes and either type the amount, let your next statement fill it in, or flag it to come back to — pending bills show on Today, the Plan and the sort cards until they have an amount.

Money plan wizard: 'Your money right now' asks for the balance of each of your four accounts (Everyday, Bills, Savings, Investment) instead of one total. 'Suggest a split' uses those balances, and the transfer step now shows what each account has today and the exact moves to make.
Money plan wizard: the transfer step now lists all four accounts, with empty ones explained instead of hidden
Reimbursements: mark an expense 'getting reimbursed', see it on Today until the money comes back, and assign any incoming amount to it in full or in part — spending nets off automatically
Split one purchase across several categories: 'Split…' on the sort card, or right-click any transaction; Analysis, the pie, the month report and pacts count each part
Sort queue: the overview now scrolls and lists every merchant (click one to start there); cards scroll so 'Make it a recurring bill' shows its fields on smaller screens

Calmer Today: the Pulse collapses to a strip once done, pacts and the monthly event fold into one section, a single quick-action row with a More menu, systems reveal themselves as you go (Settings can show everything), fewer stacked toasts and celebrations
